title: Epidemic, Endemic, and Eradication Simulations
beats: Three phases announced: epidemic, endemic, eradication
City of homes/non-homes, blobs roam up to three places daily, SIR states as colors, permanent immunity
Admits model is far simpler than reality; goal is patterns, not COVID predictions
First run: 10 infected, 1% chance; stacked graph read at day 3 with concrete counts
R-naught defined with 2-blob, R0=3 arithmetic, then exponential growth
Simulated growth is messier/faster than R0 predicts; averaged R0 is a luxury real world lacks
R0 pretends all susceptible; add S to get R; logistic growth named and deferred; R vs 1 thresholds, herd immunity
Herd immunity is not a cap: 41% infectious at peak, 85% ever infected
Rerun at R0 2.5, 1.5, 1.1, 0.9 to see peak shrink and decline below 1
Vary infectious period and population at fixed R0; viewer predicts peak, total
Timelines differ but peak and total fractions nearly identical; only R0 matters
Links R0=2.5 to early COVID estimates, so the do-nothing case is worrying
Why diseases do not die out: add lifespans and new susceptibles; R pulled back toward 1
Herd immunity = 1 - 1/R0, giving 60% at 2.5, matching quoted 50-70% range
Reminds that seasonality, mutation, reaction change real numbers; equilibrium pattern holds
Vaccinate newborn blobs at 60/50/35/20%; predict before run
Only 60% eradicates; presenter expected 50% to work; the gap to threshold lets disease wobble
Real eradication is infeasible (animals), but partial vaccination still lowers spikes

metrics.misconception: yes: herd immunity is not a cap on infections (3:34); 50% vaccination would eradicate (10:33)
metrics.brute_force: yes 1:01: simulate blobs in rooms rather than solve equations
metrics.examples: ~5 sims at R0 2.5 reused as baseline, then 4 R0 values, then 4 variants at fixed R0, then endemic, then 4 vaccination rates; each batch of four with a prediction prompt
metrics.ending: Takeaway that eradication is hard but partial vaccination still helps; charity plug

principles.1: confirmed: city, rooms, colored blobs before any formula (0:15-0:46)
principles.2: confirmed: R0 at 1:24, S and R at 2:47, logistic named but deferred at 3:02; each symbol introduced only when the sim shows the need
principles.3: not-observed: no interface to learn beyond stacked graph, explained with a day-3 reading at 1:24
principles.4: partly: SIR blobs act as concrete model, but no separate analogy-to-rigor ladder; the model itself is the analogy
principles.5: confirmed: blobs literally move between homes and rooms and infect in rooms (0:15)
principles.6: confirmed: run the simulation instead of deriving; messy results shown (2:14)
principles.7: confirmed: repeated runs with changed parameter reveal fixed-R0 invariance (5:05-6:29) and vaccination threshold (10:15-11:10)
principles.8: partly: transcript text has no speech-rate data; idea rate slows around notation (1:24-3:34) while sim segments are mostly silent runs, supporting idea-rate over speech-rate
principles.9: confirmed: R0 sweep, parameter variants, vaccination rates all use the same four-run template
principles.10: partly: first run is one scenario and sweeps follow, but there is no tiny-to-big ladder in population (1,000 to 10,000 only at 5:20)
principles.11: confirmed: R0 then R then herd immunity then endemic then vaccination, each needing the last
principles.12: confirmed: ties R0 2.5 to COVID estimates and the 50-70% herd range (6:45, 9:04)
principles.13: partly: plain language, R0 arithmetic, but tools chosen mostly as 'sim shows it' rather than justified against alternatives

new_moves.name: predict-before-batch
new_moves.what: Run four parameter variants side by side after asking for predictions on named quantities (peak, total)

new_moves.name: expected-vs-actual-gap
new_moves.what: Show that the formula's prediction and one run differ, and name why simulations matter

new_moves.name: invariance-discovery
new_moves.what: Vary irrelevant parameters to show what does not matter

theory: The video teaches by treating each formula as a patch for a visible failure of the previous one: R0 fails once immunity builds, so S appears; the epidemic ends, which is wrong, so lifespans appear. Prediction prompts before each four-run batch make the learner commit, and the presenter's own wrong guess at 10:33 models honest updating.
velocity: Scene builder: support four-run parameter grids with a pause for a typed prediction before play
Orchestrator: introduce a symbol only after a sim frame shows the previous one breaking
Evals: check that the tutor reports a case where its own expectation failed
Learner model: log predictions vs outcomes to pick which parameter to vary next
quote: I thought that 50% might do it
